title: Dark Energy as the Vacuum Energy of the MOND Field: a Consistent Model with a Turn-Off Near 1e-8 m/s^2
description: Version 1.1 (prediction 2 corrected: the turn-off is structurally out of reach of galaxy-scale data, lane p38; AI-assisted research programme; not peer reviewed). We propose that the observed dark energy is the vacuum (zero-field) energy of the field that produces MOND. In QUMOND and the nonrelativistic limit of bimetric MOND this energy is Lambda c^4/a0^2 = (1/2) int (nu - 1) d(y^2), identical in both bimetric classes and automatically de Sitter. The quadrature kernel sqrt(1 + 1/y) makes it diverge and violates the planetary ephemerides; one strong-field turn-off cures both and gives Lambda c^4/a0^2 ~ (pi/4) y_t. With measured a0 = 1.097e-10 m/s^2 the observed Lambda fixes y_t = 94 (71-117 at 2 sigma), a turn-off near 1.0e-8 m/s^2, allowed by SPARC and every inner planet. Predictions: w = -1 with a time-constant a0 (or a0 proportional to sqrt(rho_DE) if dark energy evolves); a MOND turn-off near 1e-8 m/s^2 (a signature of at most ~0.002 dex, beyond any galaxy-scale probe); no quantum zero-point origin for Lambda. The coefficient a0 = (1/2) c sqrt(G rho_Lambda) is NOT derived: a Lean proof shows it is independent of the other ingredients, and the turn-off scale is a new constant. The cold mass of cosmology is still required.
